name: AI Compute Deal Ledger
cite_as: AI Compute Deal Ledger, Regards of Wallstreet, https://www.regardsofwallstreet.com/data/ai-deals
aggregates_note: contractValueUsd sums binding capacity_lease, cloud_services, chip_purchase and build_contract rows. backstop_guarantee amounts are contingent ceilings and compute_equity amounts are stakes, so both are reported in bindingValueByType and kept out of the headline. bindingValueUsd sums every binding type. None of these figures is cash already paid.

entities.name: Undisclosed frontier AI lab (Atlas Energy Solutions)

flags.conditions: About $186.2B of the total is subject to exercisable termination rights or conditions before commencement, such as a counterparty securing financing, facilities or approvals. Excludes $150B to $175B of further arrangements with no fixed dollar commitment (mostly the extra Google TPU procurement).

deals.notes: SNAPSHOT ROW, excluded from summed aggregates: Anthropic's total committed spend of approximately $900.9B as of and after September 30, 2026, substantially all compute and infrastructure, per its 424B4. Components: $320.0B of contractual obligations at September 30 (of which $313.8B purchase commitments), $17.4B of short-term commitments, $451.2B of leases signed but not commenced, $105.7B of commitments signed after September 30 and $6.6B of short-term agreements after that date; these sum to $900.9B. About $451.6B falls before the end of 2030 and $70.7B in the twelve months after September 30, 2026. The named deals inside it have their own rows; adding this total to them would double count. Earlier figures reported from drafts ($518B, $542-567B) used narrower definitions.

flags.conditions: 15-year triple-net powered land lease of Riot's entire 332-acre Corsicana, Texas campus; Riot delivers land, power infrastructure and powered pads, and the tenant deploys compute and pays substantially all operating costs. Rent is payable on the full 910 MW irrespective of utilization. About $1.8B average annual rent including escalators; two 5-year extension options would take total value to about $54B (max_with_options_usd). Delivery in three phases: 400 MW in September 2027, 200 MW in January 2028, 310 MW in July 2028; rent on each phase starts no later than 60 days after its powered pads are delivered, so revenue_start is the first phase's delivery month, not first rent. Capital cost about $6M per IT MW; Riot funds $2M per MW and the remaining $4M per MW is reimbursed to the tenant after each phase pays rent, from non-recourse project debt, or else funded by the tenant and recovered as a rent credit. Riot's press release and 8-K name only 'a leading Frontier AI Lab'. Bitcoin Magazine reports that Riot's 10-Q names Anthropic PBC as the tenant (lease signed 2026-10-28, binding 2026-11-04); that filing could not be opened from this session, so the tenant is carried as Anthropic on a single secondary report plus Riot's statement that the Rockdale tenant is the same lab (Rockdale's tenant was identified as Anthropic by Bloomberg). Riot's portfolio total of 1,151 MW and about $38B includes this row, the Rockdale row and the AMD contract.

deals.notes: Surfaced via the EDGAR watchlist hit on Riot's 8-K filed 2026-11-04 (accession 0001104659-26-122368). Arithmetic: $28B over 15 years on 910 MW is about $2.05M per MW per year; stated $1.8B average annual rent over 910 MW is about $1.98M, consistent with a land-and-power lease and above the Rockdale row's shell-style rate. No Bloomberg, Reuters or CNBC piece was found in-session; the figures rest on the company's own release and 8-K.

flags.conditions: Five-year master equipment leases with Broadcom, including the 2026 Lease Arrangement, for TPU-based hardware deployed in data centers others operate for Anthropic; accounted for as finance leases. Rent of approximately $161.2B excluding interest over the lease lives, paid quarterly from when equipment is ready for service; part came online in 2026 and more from 2027. Non-cancelable by either party except by the lessor on default. Broadcom has assigned parts of the leases to a third party and to a special purpose financing entity, which Anthropic says did not raise aggregate rent. Recorded as chip_purchase because it is hardware acquired under finance leases, not data center space.

deals.notes: Largest single figure in Anthropic's prospectus. The number moved between drafts: Fortune's reading of the public S-1 (2026-10-26) gave $125.2B of rent for the leases; the 424B4 (2026-11-19) gives approximately $161.2B, and the row carries the 424B4 figure. No tier-1 outlet was found quoting the final figure; the second source covers the earlier draft's $161.2B Broadcom-related lease line, which matches the 424B4. Distinct from the Google CSP hosting row (anthropic-google-csp-hosting-2026-03): the prospectus lists the two as separate arrangements.

flags.conditions: CSP hosting agreement signed March 2026 and amended between May and October 2026: at least approximately $121.3B of spend between April 2026 and July 2033 regardless of usage, with a true-up if spend falls short; non-cancelable except for Google's uncured material breach. Separately, Anthropic committed to procure more TPU compute with no fixed dollar figure, estimated at $125B to $150B for delivery 2028 to 2031, which is not in this row's value. Circular: Google is an Anthropic shareholder.

deals.notes: Anthropic's largest single disclosed compute commitment, first made public in its IPO registration statement. The figure rose between drafts: Reuters reported about $111.1B from the confidential draft (2026-09-29, linked via a syndicated copy), later coverage of the public S-1 about $114.5B, and the final 424B4 (2026-11-19) gives at least approximately $121.3B after the amendments through October; the row carries the 424B4 figure. No MW is recorded, so the 1 GW on google-anthropic-tpu-2025-10 (the October 2025 TPU expansion, which may sit inside this agreement) is not counted twice. term_years 7.3 is April 2026 to July 2033.

flags.conditions: Fees accrue only as capacity is delivered and accepted; non-cancelable except for Lambda's uncured material breach or other limited circumstances and, for some agreements, per tranche if Lambda misses delivery milestones.

deals.notes: Anthropic's May and June 2026 agreements with Lambda to access Nvidia GPU compute, first disclosed in its IPO registration statement (public S-1 filed 2026-10-26). Computed: the 424B4 gives approximately $41.3B for all Lambda agreements over terms into 2034, of which the August agreement (anthropic-lambda-cloud-2026-08) is approximately $34.9B, leaving about $6.4B for May and June. Neither agreement was announced separately and no MW or start date is disclosed. The second source is the 2026-11-17 S-1/A, the same company's earlier filing, not an independent outlet; no press coverage breaking out the May and June agreements was found.

flags.conditions: Up to $120.5B over terms extending into 2029, about $3.1B a month once all capacity is delivered, which Anthropic expects in December 2026, with different fees while capacity ramps. After initial non-cancelable periods ending January 2027 and March 2027, either party may cancel each agreement on 90 days' notice, so the firm portion is far smaller than the headline. term_years 3.5 is May 2026 into 2029, approximate.

deals.notes: All of Anthropic's agreements with SpaceX.AI LLC (formerly X.AI LLC, a SpaceX subsidiary) for Nvidia GPU compute, entered and amended between May and October 2026, including the Colossus 1 rental first announced 2026-05-06 (spacex-anthropic-colossus1-2026-05, now superseded by this row). Earlier Reuters reporting on the confidential draft put the figure at up to $84.5B; the public S-1 and the final 424B4 both give $120.5B. Arithmetic: $3.1B a month is $37.2B a year, so about $120B needs roughly 3.2 years at full rate, consistent with terms running into 2029 after a ramp.

flags.conditions: Two wholly owned, indirect Atlas subsidiaries executed separate cost reimbursement agreements with an unnamed 'leading frontier AI lab', paired with equipment purchase agreements under Atlas' existing Global Framework Agreement with Caterpillar. The first reimburses balance-of-plant equipment (emissions controls, electrical distribution, battery storage) supporting Atlas' already-placed generator orders; the second reimburses an incremental 283 MW of Caterpillar power-generation equipment for the initial power ramp of a specific data center project, which is the capacity recorded here. A separate 328 MW Caterpillar generating-capacity purchase for 2027 delivery was reported alongside this announcement but described as fulfilling Atlas' pre-existing GFA obligations rather than this specific AI-lab reimbursement, so it is not included in mw_it pending clearer sourcing.

deals.notes: Surfaced via the EDGAR watchlist hit on Atlas Energy Solutions' 8-K filed 2026-09-25. No dollar value is stated anywhere in the primary 8-K or its press-release exhibit; several secondary finance-aggregator sites (Parameter.io, MoneyCheck, and syndicated BusinessWire republishes) report an aggregate '$613.5 million' figure ($340.5M balance-of-plant + $273M power generation) attributed to 'Atlas Energy's official announcement', but that figure does not appear in the SEC-filed exhibit text as fetched in this session, so it is omitted here per the figure-verification rule against unconfirmed aggregator numbers; value left null and the row qualifies on the disclosed 283 MW figure alone (inclusion criteria 3's 50 MW+ path). The AI-lab counterparty is unnamed in all sourcing found. Only one non-tier-1 secondary source was available same-day; no Reuters/Bloomberg/CNBC/WSJ/FT coverage had appeared as of this review, so re-check for a tier-1 corroboration and the dollar figure on the next run.

flags.conditions: Expanded multi-year agreement for Anthropic's CPU-based AI compute workloads on Akamai Cloud's distributed infrastructure and software, $11.6B base contractual commitment over 7 years, with an option for up to $9B in additional commitments (company describes the combined potential as 'up to approximately $20 billion'; 11.6+9=20.6, so the row's max_with_options_usd is the computed sum rather than the rounded soundbite). Revenue recognition begins H2 2027, reaching an estimated ~$1.7B annualized run rate by end of 2028. Akamai anticipates about $5.5B of its own capex tied to building out the committed capacity ($1.7B of that landing in 2026), which is Akamai's cost to fulfill the contract, not part of this row's value. Akamai granted Anthropic a warrant for non-voting convertible Series B Preferred Stock, 7.7M shares on an as-converted basis (~5% of Akamai's outstanding common stock) at an $111.33 strike; roughly 2% of that vests with the $11.6B base commitment and the remaining ~3% vests in tranches (~1% per additional $3B) as the option is exercised. Company states no impact to 2026 revenue guidance from this contract.

deals.notes: Found via web research this run; the largest deal added this week. Neither Akamai nor Anthropic (as a CPU-cloud provider relationship) was on the EDGAR watchlist under this pairing, so this surfaced only via the general web scan, not the daily EDGAR watch. Scale check: Akamai's trailing revenue is in the low-$4B/year range, so an $11.6B commitment landing over 7 years (~$1.7B/year run rate at full ramp by 2028) is large relative to the company but consistent with the company's own guidance language and the capex build it says the deal requires; this is explicitly why Akamai stock re-rated sharply on the announcement (per Yahoo Finance, TechCrunch). Cross-source: SEC 8-K exhibit (primary, Akamai's own release) plus Bloomberg (tier-1, headlining a slightly-rounded '$12 billion') and TechCrunch, both citing the same $11.6B/7-year figures as the base commitment; Bloomberg's '$12 billion' headline rounds the $11.6B base, not a conflicting figure. CPU-only workload, distinct in kind from the GPU-capacity deals that make up most of the ledger.

flags.conditions: Oracle's fiscal Q1 FY2027 results (quarter ended 2026-08-31, reported 2026-09-10) disclosed total Remaining Performance Obligations of $664B, up $209B year over year and $26B sequentially from the $638B reported at FY2026 Q4. Management said roughly half should convert to revenue within 36 months, contingent on building and delivering the contracted data-center capacity on schedule; Bank of America analysts estimate over 50% of RPO traces to OpenAI. Oracle booked more than $30B of new AI cloud contracts and delivered 850MW of additional data-center capacity in the quarter.

deals.notes: SNAPSHOT ROW, excluded from summed aggregates: Oracle's company-wide RPO across all cloud customers, not a single deal. Overlaps almost entirely with named rows already on the ledger (openai-oracle-stargate-2025-09 at $300B, meta-oracle-cloud-2025-10 at ~$20B, and other multi-billion contracts with customers Oracle has not named), so this row exists only to record the disclosure, per the same total_backlog treatment already used for sb-energy-contracted-backlog-2026-09 and coreweave-backlog-2026-08. Scale check: consistent with Oracle's own prior-quarter RPO of $638B (FY2026 Q4) and the $455B figure recorded at FY2026 Q1 in the openai-oracle-stargate row; the growth trajectory across three consecutive quarters is internally consistent. Superseded snapshot: replaces the FY2026 Q1 $455B figure referenced in openai-oracle-stargate-2025-09's notes as the most current RPO read; that row's notes are left as a historical record of the September 2025 print rather than edited, per the house rule against silent overwrites.

flags.conditions: Multi-generational custom-silicon collaboration: Qualcomm Technologies builds custom AI inference chips, server-class systems and manufacturing services for AWS, plus joint work on 1.6T+ optical connectivity. Disclosed via a Qualcomm Item 3.02 8-K covering a warrant Qualcomm issued to Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings for up to 25,000,000 Qualcomm shares at $161.26/share (expires 2036-09-03), vesting in tranches tied to Amazon placing binding purchase orders and actually buying Qualcomm's server chip products, technology, systems and manufacturing services, up to a $60B payments ceiling that triggers full vesting. 3,750,000 shares vested immediately on issuance based on an undisclosed initial purchase commitment. The $60B is the vesting ceiling, not a guaranteed minimum spend, hence the up_to qualifier; no MW or chip-count figure was disclosed. The warrant itself is separately valued at roughly $4B at issuance by multiple outlets -- that is the value of the stock grant, not the purchase commitment, and is not the figure this row carries. Qualcomm said it is already in production with Amazon and expects revenue from the relationship starting in its December 2026 quarter.

deals.notes: Qualcomm's largest push yet into AI data-center silicon, and its first hyperscaler customer for the strategy. The $60B figure is a warrant-vesting ceiling disclosed by Qualcomm itself in its 8-K, not a stated minimum purchase commitment, so it is entered with an up_to qualifier per the same treatment used for the Amazon-Anthropic and Microsoft/Nvidia-Anthropic investment rows. Found and researched 2026-09-11 but never entered: the branch that added it sat open a month and could not be merged once main's history moved past its base, so it is backfilled here with recorded set to the actual entry date rather than the research date. Re-checked against the same primary sources on 2026-10-12; nothing material had changed.

flags.conditions: SB Energy's S-1 registration statement (filed for a planned Nasdaq/Nasdaq Texas listing as SBE) discloses $439B of total backlog under binding contracts, of which approximately $430B is from data centers, against 8.8 GW-IT of signed leases concentrated in two customers: OpenAI (approximately 8.0 GW-IT across 17 buildings, 20-year leases, at the Ohio PORTS-Pike campus) and SoftBank (the balance, including the Cosmos Technology Campus in Travis County, TX: 50 MW-IT under a 15-year triple-net lease with expected aggregate rent of $2.5B, financed by $999M of 8.875% senior secured notes due 2031 issued by project subsidiary SE Cosmos LLC, first rent targeted Q4 2026). The backlog is heavily back-loaded: roughly $1B is expected to convert to revenue in the next 24 months, with about $357B beyond year 8. SB Energy reported approximately $4B of debt and a $3.8B accumulated deficit as of the filing.

deals.notes: SNAPSHOT ROW, excluded from summed aggregates (basis: total_backlog). Surfaced from the EDGAR watchlist hit on SB Energy's S-1 (filed 2026-09-01/02). This is SB Energy's own rollup of its signed data-center leases and is not additive with nvidia-openai-sb-energy-ohio-2026-08 (Nvidia's $105B residual-value guarantee on the initial 4.25 GW-IT phase of the same OpenAI Ohio lease) or with any other row: they describe different instruments (guarantee ceiling vs. lease backlog) against overlapping capacity, so summing them would double count the Ohio campus. Scale check: $439B backlog against a company with ~$4B of debt and a $3.8B accumulated deficit and no operating data center yet is consistent with the pattern already established by Stargate ($500B program envelope) and Applied Digital ($36B backlog on 1.41GW); AI-infrastructure backlogs routinely run far ahead of revenue at this stage of the cycle, and SB Energy's own S-1 states the same (~$1B converts in 24 months, ~$357B beyond year 8). Arithmetic check: $430B data-center backlog / 8.8GW-IT over the disclosed lease terms (mostly 20-year OpenAI leases) is broadly consistent with the $13.3M/MW/yr full-stack rate already reconciled for OpenAI-Oracle Stargate capacity, though SB Energy's mix includes lower-cost triple-net shell leases (the Cosmos campus alone reconciles to $2.5B / 50MW / 15yr = ~$3.3M/MW/yr, inside the ledger's sanity band). Cross-source: SEC S-1 (primary) plus independent Yahoo Finance and Latitude Media reporting citing the same $439B/8.8GW-IT/8.0GW-IT figures. Counterparty note: 'buyer' role split across OpenAI (Ohio, ~8.0GW-IT) and SoftBank (remaining balance including Cosmos); the S-1 itself does not further break out the balance by named tenant beyond SoftBank affiliates, so this row does not assert a precise split beyond the two figures given in conditions.

flags.conditions: Reported cloud-compute agreement layered on top of the existing Hut 8 Beacon Point capacity (hut8-beacon-point-phase1-2026-05 / -phase2-2026-07, Nueces County, Texas): per Bloomberg's sourcing, Anthropic pays Lambda, Lambda installs Nvidia chips at roughly 350MW of the Beacon Point campus, and Nvidia (reported, unconfirmed, as the tenant behind the Hut 8 leases) sits above the arrangement as both chip supplier and underlying facility lessee, paying Hut 8's rent. This row records the Anthropic-to-Lambda commercial layer only; it is not an expansion_of the Hut 8 rows since it is a different contract, a different counterparty pair and a different dollar figure describing a different layer of the same physical capacity, and summing it with the Hut 8 rows would double count the underlying MW. Flagged circular given Nvidia's presence on multiple sides of the same capacity chain. Term length and GPU count were not disclosed in any report found. Initial energization expected Q1 2027. Neither Anthropic, Lambda nor Nvidia has confirmed the deal; held at status reported (excluded from binding aggregates) on two independent tier-1 reports. Anthropic's 424B4 (2026-11-19): the August 2026 Lambda agreement is approximately $34.9B of a $41.3B Lambda total. Either party may terminate it if Lambda did not secure the facility lease by a set date; Lambda missed that date, so the agreement is currently terminable by either party. Neither side had given notice as of the prospectus, and Anthropic says it does not currently intend to terminate. Recorded as binding because it is a signed, definitive agreement, with this condition shown; the May and June agreements are anthropic-lambda-cloud-2026-05. capacity.mw_it cleared to null on 2026-11-20: the reported 350 MW sat inside Hut 8's Beacon Point leases, which already carry that capacity, and counting it here as well would double the GW total now that the row is binding. The prospectus also says Lambda did not secure the facility lease, so the Beacon Point link is unconfirmed.

deals.notes: Backfilled 2026-09-18 during the weekly ledger review, found alongside the Nscale row while researching Anthropic's reported $517B compute-commitment aggregate (that aggregate is not itself ledgered; it is a media rollup, not a company disclosure, and mostly restates deals already on the ledger). Second of Anthropic's two reported deals in the same week (the other being anthropic-nscale-monarch-2026-08); both stay separate rows since they name different providers, sites and figures.

revisions.reason: reported to binding on Anthropic's 424B4, which describes the signed August 2026 agreement. Value restated from $35B (Bloomberg) to approximately $34.9B (company_stated). Flagged: currently terminable by either party because Lambda missed the facility-lease deadline.
350 to null: the MW is already counted on the Hut 8 Beacon Point rows, and the facility lease the agreement depended on was not secured.

flags.conditions: Six-year, ~460MW compute capacity lease at Nscale's Monarch Compute Campus in Mason County, West Virginia (a 2,250-acre site Nscale acquired March 2026, planned for up to 8GW total, first 2GW phase targeted online H1 2028). Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, reported to come online 'late' 2027. Neither Nscale nor Anthropic has issued an official press release or SEC filing confirming the deal; it is entered at status reported (excluded from binding aggregates) rather than binding, per the ledger's rule for stories two or more tier-1 outlets independently confirm without a primary source. Nscale filed for a US NYSE listing (ticker NSCL) around 2026-09-18 and press coverage of that filing describes the Anthropic lease anchoring its contracted backlog, but as of this row's 2026-10-12 recheck no S-1/F-1 text naming Anthropic or stating deal terms could be independently located and read, so that filing is not counted as the needed primary confirmation yet. Revisit and flip to binding once the registration statement itself can be read and confirms the deal. Confirmed in Anthropic's 424B4 (2026-11-19): GPU services agreements signed August 2026 with Nscale subsidiaries, up to approximately $44.6B over terms extending into 2033, fees accruing only as capacity is delivered and accepted. Nscale must use best efforts to obtain qualifying financing for the GPUs and data center within a specified period; otherwise non-cancelable except for Nscale missing delivery or availability requirements or an uncured breach.

deals.notes: Anthropic's largest single reported compute commitment on the ledger at the time of writing, surfaced alongside the AMD and Qualcomm-Amazon gaps the week of 2026-09-11. CNBC independently corroborated Bloomberg's initial report the same day; Reuters also picked it up. Backfilled a month late for the same reason as the other rows added this run: the original branch could not be merged once main's history moved past its base. Still watching Nscale's IPO filings for primary confirmation.

revisions.reason: reported to binding: Anthropic's 424B4 describes signed GPU services agreements with Nscale. Value restated from $45B (Bloomberg, media_reported) to up to $44.6B (company_stated). deal_type capacity_lease to cloud_services, since Anthropic buys GPU services from Nscale rather than leasing space.

flags.conditions: Five-year GPU cloud services agreement via HIVE's BUZZ HPC subsidiary, built around a dedicated cluster of 2,016 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs at HIVE's hydro-powered Merritt, British Columbia facility. Company-stated total contract value ~$350M (~$70M/yr annualized revenue), against ~$185M of capex HIVE expects to spend building out the cluster. Counterparty disclosed only as 'an investment-grade enterprise customer'; no MW/IT-load figure given, so this row relies on the disclosed dollar value (clears the $100M threshold) rather than a capacity figure for inclusion.

deals.notes: Surfaced via the EDGAR watchlist keyword hit on HIVE's 8-K filed 2026-08-19. Sourcing is one primary company release plus The Block (crypto/tech trade press, not a Reuters/Bloomberg/CNBC/WSJ/FT tier-1 outlet); no independent tier-1 confirmation found. Counterparty is unnamed, following the same undisclosed-counterparty pattern already used for Hut 8, Applied Digital and Sharon AI rows -- flagged via counterparty_unnamed rather than omitted, since the dollar figure and GPU count are independently disclosed and verifiable against HIVE's own filings.

flags.conditions: Five-year hosting agreements for 55 MW of new AI data center capacity across multiple, unnamed additional U.S. sites, explicitly 'in addition to' the companies' existing 10 MW Columbus, Georgia deployment (duos-axe-compute-columbus-2026-07): a distinct, additive commitment, not a restatement of the earlier deal. Aggregate value is '$500 million+' in contractual base payments over the 5-year term, excluding electricity/usage charges -- an undiscounted multi-year total with escalators, not a single upfront payment. Initial project readiness targeted late 2026 into early 2027, subject to construction, commissioning and Axe Compute's written acceptance. The companies also signed nonbinding term sheets for Axe Compute to take minority (up to 49%) equity stakes in the project entities; that equity piece is not itself quantified in dollars and is not included in this row's value.

deals.notes: Surfaced via the EDGAR watchlist keyword hit on Duos's 8-K filed 2026-08-17. Sourcing is two primary releases (one from each counterparty, Duos and Axe Compute) plus DCD trade-press pickup; no Reuters/Bloomberg/CNBC/WSJ/FT coverage found -- flagged as thin/single-tier (primary-only) sourcing despite clearing the two-source bar. Arithmetic check: $500M / 55MW over 5 years is ~$1.8M/MW/year, well inside the ledger's $200k-$20M/MW/year sanity band and close to the $111M/10MW/5yr rate on the original Columbus deal (~$2.2M/MW/year), so the per-MW economics are internally consistent between the two rows.

flags.conditions: Nvidia entered residual value guaranties with SB Energy covering leases for approximately 4.25 GW of IT load at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus (the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant) in Pike County, Ohio, capped at $105B in aggregate; payments trigger only if OpenAI, the 20-year tenant, defaults or becomes insolvent, so the $105B is a contingent guarantee ceiling, not a committed cash outlay. Nvidia can extend further credit support to roughly 3.8 additional GW at its sole discretion (unquantified in dollars, not included in this row's value); full campus is planned at up to 8 GW by decade's end. Alongside the guaranty, Nvidia is investing $1.5B in direct equity in SB Energy (joining existing investors SoftBank Group and OpenAI); separately, SoftBank/SB Energy have committed $4.2B to regional grid infrastructure. Neither the $1.5B equity stake nor the $4.2B grid commitment is included in this row's value, which covers the lease-guarantee instrument only. First 800MW of capacity targeted online in 2028 (year-precision only; no specific month disclosed). Circular by construction: Nvidia guarantees the lease, invests equity in the landlord, and is the exclusive chip supplier hosted on the campus.

deals.notes: Surfaced via the EDGAR watchlist hit on Nvidia's 8-K filed 2026-08-17. This formalizes and supersedes the reported-only nvidia-openai-backstop-talks-2026-07 row (WSJ/CNBC talks reported 2026-07-27 of a speculative up-to-$250B backstop for a rumored 10GW campus); the signed terms differ materially ($105B not $250B; 4.25GW initial plus an unquantified 3.8GW discretionary option, not a flat 10GW; a specific 20-year OpenAI lease rather than open-ended talks), so that row's status was changed to superseded rather than deleted or merged. The single largest binding row on the ledger by guarantee ceiling. Scale check: Nvidia's own $500B multi-year compute-financing framework (nvidia-compute-financing-platforms-2026-08, announced 8-10) and its reported $250B-scale backstop talks for this same project (7-27) both preceded this at similar or larger magnitude, so $105B as the final signed number is consistent with, not an outlier against, Nvidia's disclosed scale of activity this cycle. Arithmetic check: $105B / 4.25GW = ~$24.7M per MW over the full 20-year guarantee horizon, i.e. ~$1.24M/MW/year, which sits inside the ledger's $200k-$20M/MW/year sanity band (this is a guarantee ceiling amortized over the lease term, not a services price, so it is compared loosely rather than treated as a strict services rate). Cross-source: SEC 8-K (primary) plus independent CNBC and Bloomberg reporting (tier-1), both citing the same $105B/4.25GW figures; earlier $250B/$120B figures circulating 7-27 through 8-14 were pre-signing negotiation leaks per WSJ and are explicitly superseded by the SEC-filed number.

SNAPSHOT ROW, excluded from summed aggregates: CoreWeave's quarter-end (June 30, 2026) revenue backlog reached $104B (+246% YoY) at Q2 2026 results, built up substantially from named deals already on the ledger (Meta's $21B expansion, the Anthropic agreement, Jane Street's $6B commitment). The release additionally disclosed more than $25B of net-new customer commitments signed in early Q3 2026, unattributed to any named counterparty, bringing a pro-forma total to roughly $129B; that increment is not a discrete, sourceable deal and is not reflected in this row's amount_usd. Update 2026-11-20: Q3 2026 results (2026-11-10) put revenue backlog at approximately $132.5B as of September 30, 2026, up $28.5B (27%) from $104B in one quarter and in line with the roughly $129B pro forma implied in August.

revisions.reason: Snapshot refreshed from $104B (June 30, 2026) to approximately $132.5B (September 30, 2026) at Q3 results.

flags.conditions: IBM will deploy a dedicated large-scale cluster of Nvidia HGX B300 systems (Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet networking) on IBM Cloud for Together AI's open-source model inference capacity; described as the first dedicated large-scale B300 inference cluster on IBM Cloud. Exact contract term length not disclosed beyond 'multi-year'.

deals.notes: Surfaced by this week's web sweep, not the EDGAR watchlist (IBM and Together AI are not on the watchlist). No tier-1 pickup (Reuters/Bloomberg/CNBC/WSJ/FT) found; corroborated instead by IBM's own newsroom release plus independent trade press (The Register, HPCwire, StorageReview all reporting the same $240M figure).

flags.conditions: Structured as MOUs establishing 'AI Compute Infrastructure Financing Platforms' with six asset managers, intended to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital for data centers, power and Nvidia hardware, off Nvidia's own balance sheet. Nvidia is reported to be guaranteeing residual value on the Nvidia GPUs used as collateral. No specific site, project or binding capital commitment is named; this is a formal Nvidia-initiated framework, not reported talks.

deals.notes: PROGRAM ENVELOPE / FRAMEWORK, excluded from binding aggregates: same anti-double-counting treatment as the January 2025 Stargate framework row. Discrete projects that sign under this financing platform should get their own rows (expansion_of this one where the provider or financier chain matches). Distinct from the separate, still-unverified Nvidia-SK Hynix ~$500B letter of intent (data-center investment plus HBM4 memory supply) sitting in candidates.json; do not conflate the two despite the matching headline figure. Expansion of the March 2025 agreement by up to $6.5B, taking the cumulative CoreWeave-OpenAI contract value to roughly $22.4B per CoreWeave (a figure that includes a reported May 2025 expansion of up to $4B still sitting in the candidate queue). Circular flag inherited from the parent agreement's cross-shareholding.

flags.conditions: Letter of intent, not a definitive agreement: investment staged progressively as each gigawatt of at least 10 GW of Nvidia systems is deployed. First gigawatt targeted for H2 2026 on the Vera Rubin platform.

deals.notes: NON-BINDING, excluded from binding aggregates: LOI for Nvidia to invest up to $100B in OpenAI, staged as each gigawatt of at least 10 GW of Nvidia systems deploys. The archetypal circular AI deal: the investor is the chip supplier whose systems the investment buys. Context for the July 2026 backstop talks (nvidia-openai-backstop-talks-2026-07).

flags.conditions: Neither company has press-released the $300B figure; it was reported by WSJ on 2025-09-10 and subsequently confirmed by OpenAI per CNBC. March 2026: the planned 600 MW Abilene flagship expansion was scrapped after financing talks stalled (Bloomberg), with capacity redistributed across other sites; the 4.5 GW program and the contract itself remained in effect per the same reporting.

deals.notes: The largest verified compute contract on record: OpenAI to purchase $300B of computing power from Oracle over roughly five years starting 2027, part of the Stargate program, delivered from about 4.5 GW of capacity per the July 2025 Oracle-OpenAI development agreement (Bloomberg). Corroborated by Oracle's own FY26 Q1 release the day before the WSJ report: RPO up 359% to $455B on 'four multi-billion-dollar contracts with three different customers'. Held in the candidate queue at ledger launch until a primary source and two tier-1 URLs were captured; promoted the same day.

flags.conditions: Total contract value subject to deployment and availability of the GPU services, delivered in tranches during 2025 and 2026 from the Vineland, New Jersey data center. Microsoft may acquire additional services and capacity, lifting the total to about $19.4B.

deals.notes: Five-year agreement for Nebius to provide Microsoft dedicated GPU infrastructure capacity at its Vineland, New Jersey site: about $17.4B through 2031, expandable to about $19.4B. Nebius shares jumped roughly 60% on the disclosure. Part of Microsoft's pattern of leasing third-party capacity (see also iren-microsoft-gb300-2025-11) rather than waiting on its own buildout.

flags.conditions: OpenAI pays through 2029. Disclosed on CoreWeave's Q1 2025 earnings call as an unnamed 'enterprise AI company'; the counterparty was identified as OpenAI in the regulatory filing the following day.

deals.notes: The middle link of the CoreWeave-OpenAI chain: up to $4B of additional capacity through 2029, disclosed at Q1 2025 earnings, between the March initial agreement (up to $11.9B) and the September expansion (up to $6.5B). Promoted from the candidate queue on 2026-08-03 once the Bloomberg capture pinned the date. Circular flag inherited from the parent agreement's cross-shareholding.

flags.conditions: 15-year base lease plus two five-year extension options. Capacity was committed in three tranches at Galaxy's Helios campus (Dickens County, TX): 133 MW critical IT signed 2025-03-28 (~$4.5B company-stated revenue over the 15-year term), a second 260 MW tranche signed August 2025 on similar terms, and a final 133 MW option CoreWeave later exercised, together totaling the 526 MW critical IT / 800 MW gross power CoreWeave has now committed to. Amount here uses Galaxy's own most recent combined guidance (average annual revenue 'more than $1 billion' across all three tranches, as restated in the July 2026 Phase I completion release) times the 15-year term, rather than summing the individually-announced tranche figures, to avoid double counting; treat $15B as a floor, not the company's headline number.

deals.notes: Phase I (133 MW) has been delivering revenue since rent commencement in Q2 2026. Phase II (260 MW) is expected to deliver in H1 2027, financed in part by a $3.507B senior secured note offering (Helios subsidiary, priced ~2026-07-22, 9.875% coupon due 2031); that financing is a capital-raise, not a separate compute deal, and is not its own ledger row. Total approved campus power is 1.63 GW with potential to scale to 3.6 GW; only the 526 MW CoreWeave has contracted for is counted here. Surfaced this run via the EDGAR watchlist hit on Galaxy Digital's Q2 2026 8-K (filed 2026-08-05); the underlying lease predates this run.

Initial five-year agreement of up to $11.9B for CoreWeave to deliver AI infrastructure to OpenAI, signed just ahead of CoreWeave's IPO. Flagged circular: OpenAI simultaneously became a CoreWeave investor via $350M of stock issued as part of the deal. A further expansion of up to $4B was reported in May 2025; it sits in the candidate queue until a primary source with an exact date is captured.

flags.conditions: Intent to invest $500B over four years, $100B initially, targeting 10 GW. SoftBank holds financial responsibility, OpenAI operational responsibility; initial equity funders SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX. By late 2025 the program reported nearly 7 GW of planned capacity and over $400B of investment across announced sites.

deals.notes: PROGRAM ENVELOPE, excluded from every summed total: the January 2025 Stargate announcement of intent to invest $500B over four years in US AI infrastructure. The discrete contracts inside it get their own rows as they sign, most notably the $300B OpenAI-Oracle compute contract (openai-oracle-stargate-2025-09); summing the envelope and its contents would double count by construction. Circular: the operational partner is the anchor customer of the capacity the JV builds.

flags.conditions: Doubled Amazon's total Anthropic investment to $8B; only the incremental $4B tranche is recorded on this row. Announced with AWS becoming Anthropic's primary cloud and training partner, training on AWS Trainium.

deals.notes: The earliest row in the ledger and the template for compute-linked equity: Amazon's additional $4B investment (total $8B) announced alongside AWS becoming Anthropic's primary cloud and training partner on Trainium silicon. The compute relationship this seeded later produced Project Rainier (~500,000 Trainium2 chips activated October 2025, ~1M by year-end) and the April 2026 expansion (amazon-anthropic-investment-2026-04, anthropic-aws-commitment-2026-04). Circular: the compute provider funding its own customer.
